KEY MESSAGE 1 DESCRIPTION...
Showers and thunderstorms will continue to develop this afternoon as 
a front approaches from the northwest. Convergence isn't all 
that great along the boundary, which should help keep coverage 
more scattered in nature. Still, effective shear of 30-35 kt and
MLCAPE of 500-1000 J/kg could allow some storm organization and
a couple of strong to severe storms. Damaging winds will be the
primary hazard, but lowering freezing levels to around 
8000-9000 ft and some steepening of lapse rates aloft will also 
bring a threat of hail. 

Convection will diminish toward sunset, but some of the CAMS are 
advertising another push of convection approaching from the north 
this evening that could bring additional storms in and around 
the mountains...so we'll have to be mindful of that. Otherwise, 
upsloping may allow a few showers overnight in the mountains, 
while skies clear out to the south as drier air moves in behind
the front. With the clearing skies and light winds, expect 
valley fog to develop in some areas, especially along the CT 
River. Overnight lows will be mainly in the 50s.

KEY MESSAGE 2 DESCRIPTION...
Friday will be a mostly dry and somewhat breezy day as high pressure 
begins to build in from the northwest behind today's cold front. 
Upslope flow may continue a few showers in the mountains early in 
the day, and a 500mb shortwave crossing the eastern Great Lakes and 
into southern New England was allow a shower or storm to clip 
southwestern NH...but the vast majority of the area will not see any 
precipitation. High temperatures will range from the low-mid 70s 
north to upper 70s-low 80s south.

Canadian high pressure further builds in from the northwest Friday 
night with good conditions for radiational cooling and a seasonably 
cool night. Low temperatures in the normally cooler and valley 
locations have a good chance of seeing lows in the 40s while others 
see temps in the 50s. Valley fog will again be possible. 

The high builds overhead Saturday, keeping the first part of the 
weekend dry with lighter winds and comfortable humidity. Highs will 
be similar to those for Friday with temps in the upper 70s-low 
80s for southern areas and low-mid 70s in the north. Good 
radiational cooling Saturday night could again bring lows down 
into the 40s to lower 50s. 

KEY MESSAGE 3 DESCRIPTION...

Looking ahead toward the second half of the weekend, Sunday
looks very seasonable due to high pressure nudging into our 
area for the day with temperatures approaching the low 80s away 
from the coast, but elsewhere, expect temperatures should stick to
the mid to upper 70s. Like for most of the summer, a sea breeze
will likely kick in during the afternoon hours, dropping 
temperatures a bit, near and along the immediate coastline. 
Clouds will be on the increase towards the latter half of the 
day due to an approaching system looking to bring rainfall for 
our region during the overnight hours. PoPs look relatively low 
for the majority of the day, however, they will start to 
increase as the weekend wanes. Most global models have Sunday 
nights' batch of rain move out by the start of the work week on 
Monday, although some showers could linger throughout the late 
morning hours. These models also show the low pressure center, 
which delivers our rainfall, to move south of us, delivering the
heaviest batch of rain to the north of the storm center, 
putting it right into our CWA. Most models have around one half 
to an inch or so of rainfall,for our CWA. For the remainder of 
the day on Monday, scattered showers look to be present in the 
mountainous areas in the afternoon hours with temperatures in 
the mid 70s away from the immediate coastline, with a few 
pockets of upper 60s for northern Coos, Franklin, and Somerset
counties.

Tuesday has high pressure sneaking closer to our area, 
delivering calm conditions with temperatures in the mid to upper
70s, resulting in seasonable conditions for this time of year. 
This high pressure system looks to dominate till the middle of 
the day on Wednesday, with diurnal shower and thunderstorm 
chances returning to our area during the afternoon hours. 
Thursday holds the potential for another system to approach 
with shower and thunderstorm chances once again. Long-range 
models, although subject to change, have a steady amount of 
precip returning to our area for most, if not all of the day on 
Thursday. The amount of rainfall is uncertain at this time being
this far out, but some indications are there for around a half 
an inch of rainfall again, further lowering any ongoing drought 
concerns for our area.
